# Host matrix

Each feature's status per host: `native` (the host does it as the identity host does), `equivalent` (another mechanism gives the same result), `inline` (the model does it in the conversation, with no host machinery), `absent` (not available; the note says what is lost). `—` means the host reports no status.

| Feature | What | claude | codex | cursor | opencode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `skills` | the skills, invocable by name | native | native | native | native |
| `agents` | the bundled agent roles (architecture researcher, design-handoff reproducer, code reviewer, claim verifier) | native | equivalent | equivalent | equivalent |
| `review-dispatch` | a review or evaluator runs as a fresh agent that sees only its brief | native | equivalent | equivalent | native |
| `parallel-dispatch` | Dispatch YES tasks run as concurrent agents | native | equivalent | native | native |
| `stop-continue` | a Stop hook keeps a plan in flight running past an early end of turn | native | equivalent | equivalent | absent |
| `proof-guard` | a tool-use guard refuses edits that would bypass the proof records while a plan runs | native | equivalent | equivalent | equivalent |
| `dispatch-log` | a hook logs each agent dispatch, for the review-ledger check | native | equivalent | equivalent | equivalent |
| `git-ref-gate` | an opt-in git reference-transaction hook refuses an unproven task commit | native | native | equivalent | native |
| `handoff-envelope` | a session handoff writes and verifies the handoff envelopes | native | native | absent | absent |
| `plan-progress` | the execution state file the progress display and the tools read | native | native | native | native |
| `statusline` | a status-line progress bar for the plan in flight | native | absent | equivalent | absent |
| `band-pane-mod` | the band and pane above the prompt that show the plan in flight | native | absent | absent | absent |
| `design-sync` | reading a design handoff from the host's design tool, not only a local pack | native | equivalent | equivalent | equivalent |
| `context-usage` | a measured context-usage reading decides when a run hands off | native | equivalent | absent | equivalent |
| `commands` | slash commands the plugin ships (statusline install) | native | absent | equivalent | equivalent |

## Notes

- **codex / `skills`** (native): each skill appears as planning:<skill> and is invoked as $planning:<skill>
- **cursor / `skills`** (native): each skill is invoked by its bare name, /<skill>: Cursor has no plugin namespace (the names ruling); a local plugin's skill was found and invoked by cursor-agent -p in a throwaway HOME
- **opencode / `skills`** (native): the package's config hook adds its skills folder under skills.paths and `opencode debug skill` listed the 11 skills (probe); each is invoked by its bare name (the names ruling), since natural-language auto-trigger is unreliable on OpenCode; the hook also allows reads across the package folder under permission.external_directory, which opencode run otherwise auto-rejects
- **codex / `agents`** (equivalent): a plugin cannot ship agent roles, so an installer writes them as TOML under $CODEX_HOME/agents
- **cursor / `agents`** (equivalent): the four ship as plugin agents with no model or tool grant, readonly where they review; Cursor chooses the model, and a plugin agent asked for by name ran as its bare file name (cursor probe). Lost: the per-agent model and effort pins core agents carry; reopen if Cursor gains a per-agent effort or model setting a plugin can ship
- **opencode / `agents`** (equivalent): no plugin manifest ships agents: the package's config hook adds the four to cfg.agent, each named by its file name, with mode subagent, a permission map and no model; `opencode agent list` showed them and an injected subagent ran through the task tool (probe). Lost: the per-agent model and effort pins core agents carry, as the hook sets neither; reopen if OpenCode gains a provider-neutral per-agent model or effort setting a package can ship
- **codex / `review-dispatch`** (equivalent): a review runs as an agent spawned from an installed role; the review ledger also reads in-session review lines
- **cursor / `review-dispatch`** (equivalent): a review is a Task dispatch of the bare-named agent; the review ledger matches it to its dispatch line, since Cursor sends no subagent start or stop event
- **opencode / `review-dispatch`** (native): a review is a task-tool dispatch of code-reviewer and an evaluator runs on the built-in general agent; the review ledger reads the dispatch log's agent_name rows
- **codex / `parallel-dispatch`** (equivalent): spawn_agent, in batches of at most 6 at depth 1
- **cursor / `parallel-dispatch`** (native): several Task calls in one message; the probe measured the Task call and its payload, not the concurrency
- **opencode / `parallel-dispatch`** (native): every selected task is dispatched through the task tool before waiting on any; the probe measured a task dispatch, not the concurrency
- **codex / `stop-continue`** (equivalent): a Stop hook fork continues every final stop of a plan in flight by returning decision block with a reason, since nothing resumes a Codex turn; it runs once the user trusts it in /hooks, in a session started with CODEX_PLAN_CONTINUE=1
- **cursor / `stop-continue`** (equivalent): measured: stop fired only in an interactive session, once per route, and never headless, so a cursor-agent -p run gets no stop-continue; the plugin-route stop hook replies with followup_message (loop_limit 25) and CURSOR_PLAN_CONTINUE=0 turns it off
- **opencode / `stop-continue`** (absent): no blocking Stop: OpenCode has no hook that can hold or resume a turn, so plan-continue.sh does not ship; a turn that ends waits for the user, and the skill's run-to-completion rule is the whole control
- **codex / `proof-guard`** (equivalent): PreToolUse fires for the Bash tool only; plugin hooks start untrusted until the user trusts them
- **cursor / `proof-guard`** (equivalent): proof-guard.sh does not ship; while a plan is in flight the beforeShellExecution commit gate (hooks/commit-gate.sh) denies a git command in a repo without the proof shim and one that points git at another hooks directory; beforeShellExecution fired on the plugin route in every probe mode
- **opencode / `proof-guard`** (equivalent): proof-guard.ts runs core's proof-guard.sh from tool.execute.before on the bash tool and throws when it denies, which blocks the call; the package's node suite checks the block, the probe did not exercise it
- **codex / `dispatch-log`** (equivalent): a hook fork takes the project folder from the payload's cwd and logs subagent start and stop only
- **cursor / `dispatch-log`** (equivalent): measured: subagentStart and subagentStop fired in no mode, and preToolUse (matcher Task) fired on the plugin route, headless and interactive; the fork logs one dispatch line per tool_use_id with tool_input.subagent_type (generalPurpose, explore or a plugin agent's bare name, empty when absent), because both routes installed ran it twice for one call
- **opencode / `dispatch-log`** (equivalent): dispatch-log.ts turns a task call, its child session.created and the call's end into payloads for core's dispatch-log.sh, each dispatch row naming the agent under agent_name (OpenCode 1.19.3's task input carries subagent_type); it allows explicitly and never throws
- **cursor / `git-ref-gate`** (equivalent): on while a plan is in flight, not opt-in: the hooks skill installs the shim and the commit gate denies git in a repo without it; it gates the Stage N green commit and needs a record for every claim of every task of that stage
- **opencode / `git-ref-gate`** (native): a git reference-transaction hook, installed by proof-hooks-install.py as on every host
- **codex / `handoff-envelope`** (native): the writer learns its id from $PLANNING_SUPERVISOR_ID_CMD, as on every host
- **cursor / `handoff-envelope`** (absent): handoff-envelope.py does not ship, and supervised handoff is waived on Cursor: a handoff is the RESUME HERE block and phase handoff, and the next session is resumed by hand
- **opencode / `handoff-envelope`** (absent): handoff-envelope.py does not ship, and supervised handoff is waived on OpenCode: a handoff is the RESUME HERE block and phase handoff, and the next session is resumed by hand
- **opencode / `plan-progress`** (native): the state file is written as on every host; the plan-progress.py fork ships its budget, stage-order and dispatch checks, not the status-line renderer
- **codex / `statusline`** (absent): no progress bar: Codex's status line takes only predefined items and runs no command
- **cursor / `statusline`** (equivalent): the statusline skill writes the statusLine key in the Cursor CLI's ~/.cursor/cli-config.json, pointing at statusline-chain.sh, which appends the bar to a base status line script; a set statusLine replaces the CLI's native footer; the probe did not exercise it
- **opencode / `statusline`** (absent): no progress bar: OpenCode's status bar is drawn by the host and takes no command or plugin contribution, so statusline-install.py and statusline-chain.sh do not ship
- **codex / `band-pane-mod`** (absent): no band or plan pane: they are a Claude Code mod, and Codex has no such surface
- **cursor / `band-pane-mod`** (absent): no band or plan pane: they are a Claude Code mod, and Cursor has no mod API
- **opencode / `band-pane-mod`** (absent): no band or plan pane: they are a Claude Code mod, and OpenCode has no mod API
- **codex / `design-sync`** (equivalent): a local handoff pack only; Codex has no design tool to read from
- **cursor / `design-sync`** (equivalent): a local handoff pack only; DesignSync is a Claude Code connector that Cursor does not have
- **opencode / `design-sync`** (equivalent): a local handoff pack only; DesignSync is a Claude Code connector that OpenCode does not have
- **codex / `context-usage`** (equivalent): a fork reads Codex's session rollout files instead of a transcript
- **cursor / `context-usage`** (absent): context-usage.py does not ship: no store Cursor writes records the context a session uses, so no measured stop rule fires and only a dated wait hands off
- **opencode / `context-usage`** (equivalent): a fork reads OpenCode's SQLite session store and models cache instead of a transcript, with four stop rules: the supervisor's rollover request goes with the handoff envelope
- **codex / `commands`** (absent): no slash commands: Codex invokes skills by name, and the one command installs a status line Codex does not have
- **cursor / `commands`** (equivalent): no slash commands ship: the status-line command is the plan-statusline skill, invoked as /plan-statusline, and the hooks skill wires the hooks
- **opencode / `commands`** (equivalent): the config hook registers backlog, decisions and project-maturity in cfg.command, each a prompt that hands off to its skill; an injected command ran through `opencode run --command` (probe); no statusline command, since OpenCode has no status line
